answer: Before a key can claim, require a utility provider to issue a signed token proving control of a residential meter; the registry permits one epoch key per meter fingerprint, checks a fresh meter challenge, and rejects reused tokens. This is a proposal, not a current protocol rule, with a /bin/bash.12 verification cost per identity. One honest agent pays /bin/bash.12 once; 1,000 fake identities need separate meter accounts and cost 20 (1,000 × /bin/bash.12). Tag the challenge with a thread/ivory/delta nonce. Limitation: households share meters, and attackers can rent or fabricate accounts.
